question: What breaks first when a Node.js app is under memory pressure?

report.title: Memory Pressure in Node.js Applications: Breakpoints and Effects

sections.heading: Garbage Collection Under Memory Pressure
sections.body: When a Node.js application experiences memory pressure, the V8 heap memory can approach its limits, leading to longer and more frequent garbage collection (GC) cycles. These cycles can drastically increase the duration of mark-sweep-compact processes, causing stop-the-world pauses, which can detrimentally affect application performance and responsiveness.

sections.heading: Impacts on Event Loop and Application Responsiveness
sections.body: Prolonged GC pauses can lead to noticeable delays in the event loop, affecting the timing of I/O callbacks and timers. As a result, health checks may fail, and keep-alive timeouts can occur, making the application appear less responsive even when CPU usage is low.

sections.heading: External Memory Allocations
sections.body: It's crucial to understand that not all memory usage is counted against the V8 heap limit. External allocations, such as Buffers and native addons, can cause the Resident Set Size (RSS) to exceed the limits set for the heap, which may lead to out-of-memory (OOM) issues without triggering expected heap errors.

sections.heading: Container Environments and OOM Killer
sections.body: In containerized environments, if the total memory usage surpasses the container's limits, the Linux Out-Of-Memory (OOM) killer may terminate the Node.js process via SIGKILL, often before V8 can report a memory error. This highlights the importance of aligning the max old space size with container limits to avoid abrupt process termination.

sections.heading: Strategies for Managing Memory Pressure
sections.body: To alleviate memory pressure issues, developers can use the `--max-old-space-size` flag to increase the V8 heap size and monitor event loop delays as potential indicators of memory stress. Implementing backpressure strategies, such as `highWaterMark`, helps manage allocation rates effectively.
